ordinal_model_coefficients_reading_texts.note: Slopes on standardised features (positive = pushes towards a higher level). Features are strongly collinear; read signs and sizes together, not one by one.

human_ceiling_ace_cefr_rater1_vs_rater2.note: Rater 2 scored against rater 1, both mapped to levels like the gold label; the gold label averages them, so this is a lower bound on gold-label reliability.

method.levels: A1=1 ... C2=6. '+' sub-levels (A2+, B1+, B2+) are folded into their base level. Ace-CEFR's 1-6 scores (half steps, rater averages) are mapped to the nearest level with .5 rounded down.
method.heuristic_nulls: estimated_level_95th is null when on-list plus proper-noun coverage never reaches 95%; scored as C2 and reported separately.
method.ordinal_model: Proportional-odds logistic regression, L2 penalty chosen by inner 3-fold CV on QWK from {0.1, 1, 10, 100}, median imputation (MTLD/MATTR are null under ~50 tokens), standardised. Within-dataset: stratified 5-fold CV, seed 0. Transfer: one model fitted on Cambridge + ELG reading texts (deduplicated), applied unchanged elsewhere.
method.ridge_check: RidgeCV regression on the same features, rounded and clipped to 1-6; reported as a robustness check.
method.macro_f1: Averaged over the levels present in the gold labels of that dataset.
method.baseline: Always predict the dataset's most frequent gold level (in-sample, so optimistic).
